probe.format_note: 16:9 landscape at low resolution (736x414, 1452 frames, about 320 kb/s, Pinterest re-encode: fine UI text is soft). Stereo HE-AACv2 44.1 kHz music bed: a steady soft electronic pulse (about 0.7 s between pulses, read by eye from the waveform) from 0 s, a quiet breakdown from about 16.8 s to 20.5 s, the beat back at about 20.6 s with a hit at about 22.0 s (the 'request sent' moment), full again from about 22.6 s to the end with a soft tail after 47.5 s.

mode.alt_film_mode: UI when the content package launches software, an app or a workflow
mode.why: third-party film of unknown origin: borrow the motion language and look only, never its shots one by one, its logo, its product name, its copy, its UI screens or its people (owner note); a voiceover package defaults to REEL, and the reference's own grammar is an app UI walkthrough

ignored.why: the 'Axiom' wordmark and its folded-ribbon mark and all English copy ('Bringing Data to Life', 'Get All The Banks in One Place', 'Get Information about upcoming Events', 'Connect with your Community flow the Conversation', UI labels such as 'All Transactions', 'Directory', 'Banking Industry', 'Request Sent', 'New message from …') are third-party branding and copy; never reused as text or logo

the banking dashboard content (balance '$5,756', card number and holder name, transaction rows with Spotify/Freepik, the bank list with Citibank, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Barclays, Wells Fargo, Royal Bank of Canada, Lloyds, Banco Santander, Toronto-Dominion and their logos, employee names, figures and charts) is third-party UI content and brand names; never reused, never their figures

event names, contact names and the round avatar photos of real people (message list, notification, community bubbles, call screen) are third-party content and real faces; never reused — our avatars are drawn or abstract, never photos of real people

method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2 at 480 px (9 sheets, all viewed; frame time = (sheet-1)*6 + index*0.5 s); scene detect gt(scene,0.3): hard cuts only at 15.10 and 27.80 s (every other change is a camera move, a colour burst, a slide or a soft cut the detector does not flag); dense sheets fps=10 at 320 px over 3.2-4.8, 14.4-16.0, 26.8-28.4 and 34.0-35.6 s (4 sheets, all viewed); audio waveform (showwavespic) for the music shape. Spans away from the dense windows are read from the 0.5 s sheets, so they are accurate to about ±0.25 s; inside the dense windows to about ±0.1 s. Colours read by eye, not sampled.

shots.shot: wide, empty near-white frame: one headline line typed in the centre
shots.moves: 0.3-1.4 s the line types in character by character with a thin blinking caret (about 12-14 characters per second, linear); about 1.4-1.7 s the whole line scales down to about 45% while typing continues (smooth ease-in-out); 1.8-2.0 s the last word completes in a violet-to-blue gradient with a soft lavender glow halo behind it; 2.0-2.5 s the other words fade to grey and out from the start of the line, leaving only the keyword centred

shots.transition_out: no cut: the keyword stays and becomes the target of the next action
shots.palette: white to faint lavender, dark grey type, violet-blue gradient keyword, lavender glow
shots.built: code-native (typed text, CSS gradient text, blurred glow)
shots.reusable: yes: type the question → shrink → keep only the one word that matters, glowing; motion only, never their words

shots.shot: wide, the glowing keyword alone in the centre of the white frame
shots.moves: 2.5-3.0 s a hand cursor glides in from below to the keyword (smooth ease-out); 3.0-3.8 s hover hold, the glow pulses softly; 3.9 s click (cursor dips, glow brightens); 3.95-4.2 s a soft violet four-point burst (blurred star/blob) expands from the click point and floods the whole frame with the violet gradient (about 0.25 s, strong ease-out)

visual_language: A calm, airy app walkthrough told by a cursor. Medium: flat, clean UI windows and cards plus light kinetic type, built in code, with 2.5D moments where the flat window or cards are placed in real perspective (the swooping fly-in, the cards flipping down into a stack) and depth of field on floating round tokens. Typography: a light geometric sans for headlines, typed character by character with a caret on white scenes, or rising/unblurring word by word on gradient scenes; one keyword per line in a violet-to-blue gradient with a soft lavender glow halo; white semibold sans for the split-layout headline. Rhythm: 13 shots in 48.6 s, average about 3.7 s, with one long 8 s take (the menu drill-down); only two hard cuts (15.1 and 27.8 s); everything else is carried by camera moves, slides, morphs and a colour burst; moves are smooth and unhurried (camera moves 0.4-1.8 s, ease-in-out), UI reactions are quick (0.15-0.3 s ease-out, small overshoot on confirmation chips); cuts are not tightly locked to the steady music pulse, except the success chip on the music hit at about 22 s. Structure: chapters, each opened by a typed or revealed line with one glowing keyword, then the cursor shows that chapter inside the UI. Transition kit: colour burst from a click, perspective swoop, slide, shared-element morph (row → card, pop-up → state card), push in / pull back, white ↔ gradient hard cut, blur cut, dissolve. Palette: near-white scenes alternate with a soft lavender-violet-pink gradient-mesh background; one blue-violet accent; small green/red only as UI status. Signature moments: the typed line that shrinks to one glowing word, the click on that word bursting into the gradient world, the window swooping in on a tilt, the cascade of cards flipping into a stack, the push in to the success chip, and the logo built from a single bending bar.
look: 2.5D, not real 3D: flat UI windows, cards and type placed on planes in true perspective for the fly-in and the flipping cards; soft, low-contrast lavender drop glows under windows and cards instead of hard shadows; windows have a thin pale-lavender rim and rounded corners; glow halo behind keywords; depth of field only on the floating round tokens (near ones large and blurred) and lightly on the near edge during the swoop; background is either near-white with a faint lavender tint or a slowly drifting gradient mesh of large blurred blobs (white core, lavender, violet, pink corners), no ground plane, no texture, no grain.
code_translation: Code-native. Built in HTML/CSS/SVG in headless Chromium: a gradient-mesh background from several large blurred radial blobs drifting slowly; typed text with a caret using the shaped brand Persian font, typing whole joined glyph runs (word by word or by grapheme on a shaped string), never breaking Persian joining; keyword in gradient-filled text with a blurred copy behind as glow; CSS 3D (perspective, rotateX/rotateY) on a UI-plane div for the swooping fly-in and for the cards flipping down (rotateX 90° → 0, transform-origin top); shared-element morphs by animating one element's box from the row to the card; colour burst as a scaled, blurred SVG shape from the cursor point; depth of field on tokens as per-token CSS blur by depth; cursor as an SVG hand sprite on a path with eased moves and a click dip. Nothing here needs a real 3D render.
continuity: Chapter opener: each new topic starts on a clean white frame with one typed line ending in a single glowing keyword, then everything except that keyword falls away.
The click opens the world: the cursor clicks the kept keyword and a colour burst grows from the click point to fill the frame with the next scene.
A visible cause for every change: one cursor travels through the scenes and every UI change follows its click (menu opens, panel swaps, chip pops).
Shared-element morph: the chosen item leaves its list and grows into its own card, or a pop-up grows into its next state, so the cut is one continuous shape.
Results arrive as a cascade: items flip down one by one and stack, and the finished stack is then carried into the window that forms around it.
Detail ↔ whole: the camera pushes in to the one element that matters, then pulls back until the whole system sits small in the centre.
Drill-down: a long held shot where a menu opens level by level while the headline stays still, narrowing a choice step by step.
Light ↔ gradient alternation: near-white type scenes and lavender gradient UI scenes swap at the hard cuts, the gradient world always entered through a click, a burst or a blur.
Bookend by build: the film ends with the mark built from one simple line that bends into shape, then the name revealed beside it.
risks: Third-party film of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy the 'Axiom' logo or wordmark, the English copy, the banking screens, the balance or card figures, the bank names and logos, the people's names, the real-face avatar photos, or the shot order one by one.
Low-resolution source (736x414): fine UI text was unreadable and spans away from the dense windows are ±0.25 s; motion timing is reliable, small detail is not.

Source is 16:9 landscape; a 9:16 film must rebuild each composition vertically (headline above the UI instead of a left/right split, the UI column already tall and suited to 9:16, the card stack and floating tokens filling the height, all inside the 9:16 safe zone).

The reference reads left to right (typing from the left, caret on the right, headline at left with UI at right, slides to the left): direction for Persian follows references/rtl-grammar.md — type from the right, headline on the right in split layouts, the cursor reading right to left.
Character-by-character typing must not break joined Persian letters; type by whole words or by graphemes on an already shaped string, and the glowing keyword must be a whole word.

Typed lines and word reveals are fast and the long take holds its headline for 8 s while small UI moves: Persian hold times and minimum text sizes win over the pace (readability ranks above the reference); small UI labels are texture only and never carry meaning the viewer must read.
Avatar bubbles and the call screen use photos of real people; any people in our film are drawn or abstract tokens, never real faces (buildable-share warning for real photos/faces).

Reference colours (near-white lavender, lavender-violet-pink gradient mesh, blue-violet keyword gradient, saturated blue card) map onto brand colour roles (light background, gradient background, primary, accent); never used as literal hex values. Colours were read by eye, not sampled.
The reference uses a steady music bed with few locked cuts; our cuts follow the voiceover first, and L6 places accents on our cuts rather than reusing their music.
